events.title: Saladin Recaptures Jerusalem
events.description: After a siege of less than two weeks, Jerusalem surrendered to the Muslim forces of Saladin. The city had been under Crusader rule for almost ninety years. Saladin's terms were relatively merciful. Many residents could ransom themselves and leave.
events.significance: The fall of Jerusalem shook Christian Europe and led directly to the Third Crusade. It also made Saladin a legendary figure in both Islamic and Western history.

events.title: Mohandas Gandhi Is Born
events.description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born in Porbandar, in western India. He trained as a lawyer and went on to lead India's independence movement through nonviolent civil disobedience.
events.significance: Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolent resistance inspired civil rights and freedom movements around the world. His birthday is marked as Gandhi Jayanti in India and as the International Day of Non-Violence worldwide.

events.title: Peanuts Makes Its Debut
events.description: Charles M. Schulz's comic strip first appeared in seven American newspapers. It introduced readers to Charlie Brown, Snoopy and their friends.
events.significance: Peanuts ran for nearly 50 years and became one of the most beloved and influential comic strips ever made. It shaped popular culture through its characters, humor and gentle philosophy.

events.title: Guinea Declares Independence from France
events.description: After voters rejected a proposed French community arrangement in a referendum, Guinea declared full independence. It was the only French colony in Africa to refuse the arrangement.
events.significance: Guinea's bold break helped inspire the wave of African independence that followed in 1960 and after. It also set an early example of rejecting continued colonial ties.

events.title: The Twilight Zone Premieres on CBS
events.description: Rod Serling's anthology series debuted with a mix of science fiction, fantasy and sharp social commentary. Each episode ended with a twist.
events.significance: The show changed what television storytelling could do. It used speculative tales to explore prejudice, fear and human nature, and it influenced generations of writers and filmmakers.
